Style-based formatting and parsing rely on locale-sensitive patterns which may change depending on the Java runtime. Specifically, applications that rely on date, time, or number parsing and formatting may encounter incompatible changes in behavior when running on JDK 20 or higher.
Using an ISO standardized format or a concrete pattern that you control allows for reliable system-independent and locale-independent parsing and formatting of date, time, and number values.
, the use of fallback patterns can also help to address compatibility issues.
